claim: Blood (NBlood's InitMirrors) draws through a room-over-room stack only if the upper sector's floor wears a mirror tile (kMirrorTile or the mirror range) or has floorstat bits 0x180; an ordinary floor over a linked sector is drawn as itself. The lower sector's ceiling needs nothing: InitMirrors gives it the mirror tile when it lacks one.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/mirrors.cpp:494-503 (InitMirrors: a stack is built only when the upper floor passes IsRorSector; a lower ceiling that does not is set to kMirrorTile)
use: Give the upper sector's floor the mirror tile (504); the lower ceiling may wear it too but the engine forces it. rules_blood's stack-portal-wears-the-mirror-tile reports either half without 504.

checked.how: mirrors.cpp:243-256 IsRorSector: floor or ceiling picnum in mirrorPicStart..mirrorPicEnd (2 if stat & 0x180, else 1), == kMirrorTile (1), or stat & 0x180 (2), else 0. InitMirrors (426): 494 a stack is made only when the upper sector's FLOOR passes IsRorSector; 502-503 if the lower sector's ceiling does not, its ceilingpicnum is forced to kMirrorTile. So only the floor half must wear it.
